name: 'There is a question in it' (wa-fīhi naẓar)
definition: The commentator's polite way of saying that a view just quoted is open to objection, usually followed by the objection or left for the reader to find.
body: Commentaries and glosses have a small vocabulary of judgement that a reader must know. Wa-fīhi naẓar, 'there is a question in it', signals doubt; taʾammal, 'reflect', or fa-tadabbar, 'think it over', points to a difficulty the author does not spell out; wa-huwa ḍaʿīf, 'it is weak', and wa-huwa wahm, 'it is a slip', are sharper. A gloss may add 'its point is that…' (wajhuhu) to explain why a doubt was raised at all.
In the madrasa these words are part of reading: a student who passes over a fīhi naẓar has not yet read the line.

examples.text: 'And there is a question in it': the view just quoted is doubted.
'So reflect': there is more in the line than it says.
